evidence.experimental_conditions: Test product: night cream containing 4% methyl glucose sesquistearate. 15 µL on filter paper disc in Finn chamber. Induction: 48-hour patches (Monday and Wednesday) and 72-hour patches (Friday) applied 3 times per week for 3 weeks to left upper back. Reactions scored 15–20 minutes after removal. Challenge: 48-hour patches applied at old and new site; scored 30–35 minutes after removal, then 24 and 48 hours later. Participants: 110 adult volunteers (103 completed).
evidence.support_text: A human repeated insult patch test (HRIPT) was conducted on 110 adult volunteers to evaluate the skin sensitization potential of a night cream containing 4% methyl glucose sesquistearate. Induction: 15 µL on filter paper in Finn chamber, applied 3 times per week for 3 weeks (48h Monday/Wednesday, 72h Friday). Challenge: 48-hour application at old and new site. No adverse effects were observed during induction or challenge. The product was concluded to be neither a skin irritant nor a sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10% or 20% in DEP or EtOH:DEP (3:1); approximately 2800 volunteers across 27 studies
evidence.support_text: Induction of dermal sensitization was measured by standard human repeat-insult patch tests (HRIPT) and maximization tests in approximately 2800 male and female volunteers for 11 of the macrocyclic lactone and lactide derivatives. Of these materials, only ethylene brassylate had results indicating sensitization. Multiple HRIPT sensitization studies performed with ethylene brassylate at 10% or 20% in DEP or EtOH:DEP (3:1) have been identified. Of these 27 HRIPT studies, 25 indicated no evidence of sensitization; however, slight to mild irritation was reported. Of the remaining two HRIPT studies, one reported 2 of 107 sensitized (1.9%) and one reported 2 of 67 sensitized (3%). Therefore, among all the HRIPT studies performed with ethylene brassylate, there were 4 of 2059 positive reactions (0.19%.).
